thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Rally To Close Higher As S&P 500 Logs First 3-day Win Streak In 6 Weeks

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Rally To Close Higher As S&P 500 Logs First 3-day Win Streak In 6 Weeks
text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch , Chris Matthews
Hopes for a resolution to the U.S.-China trade spat may help to extend the rally
U.S. stocks rallied to close higher Thursday, with the S&P 500 gaining for its third straight session for the first time in six weeks, on cautious optimism that U.S.-China trade tensions could ease in the near term.
How did the benchmarks fare?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 264.98 points, or 1.1%, to 25,380.74, while the S&P 500 gained 28.63 points, or 1.1%, to 2,740.37. The Nasdaq Composite Index added 128.16 points, or 1.8%, to 7,434.06.
On Wednesday, stocks rallied but ended up weaker for the month, with the S&P 500 shedding 6.9% for its biggest monthly decline since September 2011. The Dow dropped 5.1% in its biggest monthly percentage fall since January 2016, and the Nasdaq was the worst-performing major benchmark, sliding 9.2% for the biggest fall since November 2008.
Read:After a 673-point, 2-day surge for the Dow, is the worst over for the stock market? (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/its-the-crucial-wall-street-query-is-the-worst-over-for-the-stock-market-after-an-ugly-october-2018-10-31)
What drove the market?
Stocks added modestly to their gains after President Donald Trump, in a Thursday morning tweet, hinted at progress in early trade talks with China.
(https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/1057997981922873344)
Worries about tariffs remain among investors' biggest concerns, with U.S. and Chinese leaders set to meet later in November in attempt to resolve differences that have festered into a tit-for-tat trade clash that many corporate leaders say has increased the costs of goods and services.
Larry Kudlow, Trump's top economic adviser, told CNBC in an interview on Wednesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/kudlow-its-possible-new-tariffs-wont-be-imposed-on-china-2018-10-31) that a full slate of tariffs on all of Chinese imports may still be avoided: "Nothing is set in stone right now." He said any additional tariffs would be the result of "policy talks," not any "arbitrary timeline."
Apple's (AAPL) quarterly results could also help to solidify a tenuous resurgence of bullish sentiment among investors following a bruising period. The iPhone maker's results could play a bigger-than-expected role in influencing sentiment given that the so-called FAANG, an acronym representing a quintet of technology and internet-related stocks including Apple, Facebook Inc. (FB), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) , Netlfix Inc. (NFLX) and Google-parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) , have been at the center of the recent market turmoil that drove the Nasdaq into correction territory for the first time in two years. Apple stock was up 0.8%.
On Wednesday, upbeat results from Facebook were partly credited with providing some upward thrust (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-stock-ticks-up-after-earnings-beat-revenue-miss-2018-10-30) after the social-media giant delivered a report that wasn't as bad as Wall Street feared.
What stocks were in focus?
Spotify Technology S.A. (SPOT) skidded 5.7% after the streaming music company missed analysts' estimates for total monthly active users and revenue per user.
DowDuPont Inc. (DWDP) shares jumped 8.1% following the release of third-quarter earnings that beat profit expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dowduponts-stock-jumps-after-earnings-beat-new-3-billion-stock-buyback-program-2018-11-01). The firm also announced a new $3 billion stock buyback program.
Shares of Wayfair Inc. (W) dove 13% after the firm posted (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wayfair-reports-wider-than-expected-loss-but-revenue-tops-views-2018-11-01) a wider-than-expected third-quarter loss.
Newfield Exploration Co. (NFX) shares rallied 16% after Encana Corp. (ECA)said it would buy the firm (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/encana-to-buy-newfield-in-a-55-billion-deal-2018-11-01) in a stock swap that values Newfield at $27.36 a share, or a 35% premium.
Abiomed Inc. (ABMD) stock rose 11% after the firm announced 37% revenue growth in the second quarter of fiscal 2019.
Shares of Hanesbrands Inc. (HBI) tumbled 5.5% after the firm missed third-quarter revenue estimates (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hanesbrands-shares-slide-after-sales-miss-2018-11-01).
Teva Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (TEVA) stock advanced 15% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/teva-stock-surges-6-on-q3-beats-upbeat-guidance-2018-11-01) after the company reported better-than-expected earnings.
Wynn Resorts Ltd. (WYNN) shares soared 12% following an SEC filing that indicated that the firm will take out a $500 million loan that will be used in part to buy back stock.
Church & Dwight Co. (CHD) climbed 9.3% after the consumer goods company beat profit and revenue expectations for the third quarter (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/church-dwight-raises-guidance-as-sales-rise-7-2018-11-01) while raising its full-year guidance.
What economic data were in the spotlight?
The ISM manufacturing index fell to a six month low of 57.7% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ism-manufacturing-index-falls-to-six-month-low-in-october-as-price-rises-shortages-weigh-2018-11-01) versus economist expectations of 58.7%, according to a MarketWatch poll. Respondents cited rising costs as a concern. The IHS Markit final U.S. Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index printed at 55.7 for October, up slightly from 55.6 in September. A reading of at least 50 indicates improving conditions.
Nonfarm productivity growth grew at a 2.1% annualized rate in the third quarter (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-productivity-climbs-22-in-third-quarter-2018-11-01) versus the 2% consensus estimate, according to FactSet. Unit labor costs rose by 1.2%, versus expectations of 1.1%.
The number of newly unemployed Americans seeking jobless benefits fell in the seven days ended Oct. 27 to 212,000 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jobless-claims-fall-2000-to-214000-in-late-october-2018-11-01), a touch more than the 210,000 expected by economists surveyed by MarketWatch. This figure remains at historically low levels.
What were analysts saying?
Jeff Carbone, co-founder of Cornerstone Wealth Group, told MarketWatch that "we're seeing a bottoming process" after a very difficult month for stocks, but that investors will remain cautious in the face of unknowns like the upcoming midterm elections and trends in trade policy. "You saw markets react to the president's encouraging tweet this morning," he said, which indicates that investors are hopeful that a resolution to the trade conflict could come soon.
"The midterms are having more of an effect than many people realize," he added, arguing that a Democratic takeover of the House of Representatives, and the resulting subpoena power, could lead to more investigations of the president and greater political instability in the U.S.
"Equity markets were a sea of green yesterday, as risk appetite remained supported for another day. White House economic adviser Kudlow said that more tariffs on China are not 'set in stone', which may have boosted somewhat further market sentiment," wrote Charalambos Pissouros, senior market analyst at brokerage and investment firm JFD Brokers, in a research note.
How were other markets trading?
Asian stocks generally rose, (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nikkei-lags-but-other-asian-markets-gain-to-open-november-2018-10-31) with only the Nikkei losing ground to fall 1%, and European stocks were higher.
Oil reversed direction to trade higher after October registered as the commodity's worst month in two years (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/crude-oil-tips-higher-but-is-about-to-log-a-9-october-retreat-2018-10-31). The dollar index slumped, while gold prices settled higher.
--Mark DeCambre contributed to this report
